newsitem.title: POLAND: Daewoo to change Polish car part import rules.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo to change Polish car part import rules.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Motor Co will change rules for importing parts used for car assembly at its Polish plants, a move it expects to appease a European Union protest, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

Daewoo-Poland's spokesman Andrzej Uszynski said that under new regulations, effective from March 15, car bodies, engines and transmissions would be brought in for assembly in separate transports and not in one as is the case now.

The European Commission has criticised the deal between Poland and Daewoo, which allowed the South Korean firm to import hundreds of thousands of car kits duty-free for easy assembly as part of its purchase last year of the FSO car plant in Warsaw.
EU manufacturers have said this amounts to free car imports giving a major Asian rival a back-door entry into Europe and breaches the spirit of Poland's association agreement with the union.
"From what we know from our contacts with the (Polish) government's and EU's officials there should be no EU objections to our new regulations," Uszynski said.
Uszynski also said the new import rules should help his company achieve the 1997 output target of 150,000 units. Last year, Daewoo assembled about 98,000 cars at its plant in Warsaw.
